sentences.text: The genus name Mistralazhdarcho merges the name of the local Mistral wind with the related genus Azhdarcho.
The specific name maggii commemorates Jean-Pierre Maggi, the mayor of Velaux who backed the excavation efforts.
A distinctive feature is a raised bump on the midline of the lower jaw, a trait shared with the genus Alanqa.
The holotype, which serves as the specimen the species is based on, is a partial skeleton found on a five-square-meter area within a larger fossil deposit.
The species Mistralazhdarcho maggii was formally named and described in 2018 by Valentin, Vullo, Garcia, Godefroit, and Cincotta.
Based on a humerus length of 19 centimeters, estimates using different formulas suggest a wingspan between 424 and 485 centimeters.
Since the holotype was not fully grown, adult individuals are thought to have reached wingspans of 5 to 6 meters.
Mistralazhdarcho was assigned to the family Azhdarchidae in 2018, though no precise cladistic analysis was performed at that time.
Later studies have placed the animal in different subfamilies, with one 2021 study by Brian Andres identifying it as the sister taxon of Aerotitan in Azhdarchinae.
This reptile lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous, specifically within the Campanian stage from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
It holds the distinction of being the first pterosaur named from the Campanian to Maastrichtian of Western Europe.
The phylogenetic placement of Mistralazhdarcho varies depending on the study.
